content: Twinrix is a vaccine designed to provide protection against both hepatitis A and hepatitis B. It is administered in a series of three doses. The name Twinrix reflects the combination of two previously developed vaccines: Havrix, which is an inactivated-virus vaccine for hepatitis A, and Engerix-B, a recombinant vaccine for hepatitis B. According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), clinical trials demonstrated the following levels of immune protection against hepatitis A and hepatitis B one month after each dose of Twinrix: For hepatitis A: After the first dose: 93.8% of individuals developed protective antibodies. After the second dose: 98.8% of individuals developed protective antibodies. After the third dose: 99.9% of individuals developed protective antibodies. For hepatitis B: After the first dose: 30.8% of individuals developed protective antibodies. After the second dose: 78.2% of individuals developed protective antibodies. After the third dose: 98.5% of individuals developed protective antibodies. GlaxoSmithKline, the manufacturer of Twinrix, has reported that its studies found approximately 70% of individuals developed antibodies against hepatitis B as early as one month after receiving the first dose of the vaccine. It is important to note that Twinrix, Havrix, and Engerix-B are all registered trademarks of GlaxoSmithKline. If a similar vaccine is produced by another manufacturer, it will be marketed under a different name.
